name: Star fruit (carambola)
short: Case reports and case series describe nerve and kidney poisoning after star fruit, mainly in people with kidney disease; 22-24% of reported patients died. Cases also occurred with normal kidneys.
text: The evidence is case reports and case series. A systematic review of them documented 123 patients from eight countries with star fruit toxicity, of whom 28 (22%) died; it notes reports of nerve toxicity in people with chronic kidney disease and some evidence of acute kidney injury in people with apparently normal kidney function, and concludes that people with undiagnosed kidney conditions could also be at risk. A second review of 126 reported patients found that hiccups were the most common symptom (65%) and that confusion and seizures were the symptoms most associated with death; overall mortality was 24%, with no deaths among patients with normal kidney function, 36% among those with chronic kidney insufficiency and 27% among those on dialysis, and the patients with normal kidney function had eaten substantially more of the fruit. A narrative review of 136 reported individuals, 69.1% of whom had prior kidney impairment, described acute oxalate kidney damage on biopsy and nerve effects ranging from hiccups to status epilepticus, and says both kinds of toxicity have been reported in people with abnormal and with previously normal kidney function. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
